sentences.text:
Author: T. Vinod Kumar
Bench: T. Vinod Kumar
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice T. Vinod Kumar
 Writ Petition No.13532 of 2023
Order:

This Writ Petition is filed for issuance of a Writ of Mandamus to declare the inaction of respondent No.3 in taking action against respondent No.4 despite petitioners' complaint dated 10-04-2023 through respondent No.5 and representation dated 02-05-2023 as illegal, arbitrary, unjust and violative of Article 14 of the Constitution of India.

2. Despite the name of learned counsel for the petitioners being shown in the cause list, there is no representation on behalf of the petitioners, and thus, this Court has perused the affidavit filed in support of the Writ Petition and noted the contents thereof.
3.

Heard learned Government Pleader for Municipal Administration and Urban Development appearing on behalf of respondent No.1, Sri M.Durga Prasad, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3, Sri G.Arun Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No.4 and Sri B.Siva Keshava Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.5, and perused the record.

4. The case of the petitioners, as set out in the affidavit in brief is that 1st petitioner is the absolute owner and possessor of plot R/o.4-200/1A, Eshwaripuri Colony, Sainikpuri, Kapra, Medchal- Malkajgiri District, Secunderabad, and similarly petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the absolute owners and possessors of their respective properties situated in Sanikpuri, Secunderabad, within the layout of Armed Forces Officers' Cooperative Housing Society Limited, Sainikpuri, Secunderabad.
5.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Petitioners further contend that the 4th respondent, who is the owner of plot No.B-145 of the aforesaid Society, had leased out his property to a third party for running a restaurant/cafeteria and the said third party is undertaking constructions for commencing of commercial operations from the premises/plot which is a residential colony.
6.

Petitioners further contend that on noticing the 4th respondent undertaking the aforesaid activity, they had initially submitted a representation/complaint on 07-04-2023 to the 5th respondent-Association through which the lay-out developed and plots therein having been sold to its members.

sentences.text: 1 7. Petitioners further contend that the 5th respondent, on the basis of the aforesaid representation submitted by them, had addressed letter dated 10-04-2023 to the 3rd respondent and requested the 3rd respondent not to permit any commercial activity and also not to give any permission/license in favour of the 4th respondent.

8. Petitioners further contend that despite they approaching the 5th respondent and submitting letter dated 07-04-2023, on the basis of which the 5th respondent making a request to the 3rd respondent vide letter dated 10-04-2023 not to grant any permission in respect of the subject property, the 4th respondent has illegally started the work of setting up a cafeterias as well as restaurant causing disturbance to the petitioners, who are residents of that locality.

9. Petitioners further contend that the 3rd respondent, in spite of receiving letter/representation from the 5th respondent dated 10-04-2023, did not initiate any action against the unauthorized structures being laid by the 4th respondent and as such, the petitioners once again submitted a representation dated 02-05-2023 to the 2nd respondent bringing to the notice of the said authority the unauthorized and illegal construction being made by the 4th respondent, and in spite of the same, no action is taken and hence, the present Writ petition.

10. When the Writ Petition was taken up for hearing on 27-07-2023, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.2 and 3, by placing written instructions under the signature of 3rd respondent, had stated that the respondent authorities have demolished the illegal and unauthorized structures raised by the 4th respondent on 24-06-2023 duly taking police assistance and photographs taken during the course of demolition of unauthorized structures.

This Court on the aforesaid statement being made, had noted that since the respondent authorities claim to have demolished/removed the unauthorized temporary structures, further directed the respondent authorities to verify whether any unauthorized temporary structures are still to be removed and file counter- affidavit by the next date of hearing.

11. On 27-07-2023, though this Court directed the respondent authorities to file counter-affidavit,
no counter-affidavit is filed till date.
12. On the other hand, the 4th respondent, who is alleged to have been making unauthorized and illegal constructions, has filed counter-affidavit.
13. By the counter-affidavit, the 4th respondent claims that as per G.O.Ms.No.288 dated 03-04-2008, restaurants/eating places are permitted in the residential zone.

14. The 4th respondent further claims that he had obtained registration certificate number under the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India as issued by the Government of Telangana and also obtained certificate of registration from the Labour Department and as such, the setting of cafeteria/canteen in the subject premises cannot be objected to by the petitioners.
15.

16. I have taken note of contentions urged.

17. Though the 4th respondent had placed reliance on G.O.Ms.No.288 dated 03-04-2008, it is to be noted that the aforesaid Government Order has been amended/rescinded by issuing G.O.Ms.No.162 dated 07-04-2012.

Further, by issuing G.O.Ms.No.7, there has been amendment to G.O.Ms.No.162,
which underwent further amendments vide G.O.Ms.No.50 dated 22-04-2019.
18.

Thus, the reliance placed by the 4th respondent on G.O.Ms.No.288 dated 03-04-2008 in order to claim such activities are permitted in a residential area, is totally misconceived and cannot be accepted, more particularly in absence of the 4th respondent obtaining any permission/sanction from respondent authorities for undertaking construction, even if it is a temporary structure.

19. Further, on 27-07-2023 since respondent Nos.2 and 3, had made a statement to this Court of the respondent authorities removing the illegal and unauthorized temporary structures raised by the 4th respondent, this Court is of the view that since the said unauthorized and illegal construction made by the 4th respondent having been removed, the grievance of the petitioners in the present Writ Petition stands redressed.
20.

However, in the event of any unauthorized temporary structure is existing wherein the 4th respondent is undertaking business activity of running cafeteria/canteen by constructing any temporary structure without obtaining valid permission or sanction from the respondent authorities, the respondent authorities are required to take action against unauthorized and illegal construction, since the said temporary structure would also fall within the definition of 'building' as defined under Section 2(3) of the Greater Hyderabad Municipal Corporation Act, 1955.
21.
Subject to above observations and direction, the Writ Petition is disposed of.
No costs.
22. As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending if any shall stand closed.
